# "Lower" (narrowly defined) taxa share derived traitss

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.9\linewidth]{images/apomorphies.png}
\end{figure}  

- Basal traits: evolved earlier; shared by all
- Derived traits: evolved later; define subclades

\hfill \tiny ([Berkeley: Understanding Evolution](https://evolution.berkeley.edu/evolution-101/the-history-of-life-looking-at-the-patterns//))

# When does morphology fail?  

- Plumage can converge because of biotic interactions like mimicry
- E.g., Hairy Woodpecker (*Leuconotopicus villosus*) and Downy Woodpecker (*Dryobates pubescens*)

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.5\linewidth]{images/hairydowny1.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Weibel & Moore 2005) 

# When does morphology fail?  

- Genetic data confirms analysis of traits other than plumage in Hairy / Downy pair 

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = \linewidth]{images/hairydowny2.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (Miller et al. 2019)

# Avian phylo\underline{genomics}: Hacket et al. 2008

- Passerines sister to parrots
- Flamingos sister to grebes

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width = 0.4\linewidth]{images/hackett.png}
\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (169 species, 32 kilobases, Hacket et al. 2008)  

# Avian phylo\underline{genomics}: Jarvis et al. 2014

- Neoaves diversifies at K-Pg Boundary

\end{figure}  

\hfill \tiny (48 species, whole genomes, Jarvis et al. 2014)

# Things to know

Name representative taxa from the following groups: 

- Paleognathae and Neoaves
- Galliformes and Anseriformes
- Aequiornithes 
- "Basal" Neoaves (Camprimulgiformes, Columbiformes, Gruiformes, Hoatzin)

Remember:

- How taxonomy and phylogenetics are related
- Relationships in basal Neoaves are hard to determine due to rapid radiation at K-Pg boundary
- Australaves contains parrots, falcons, passerines
